chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one who performs Tawaf after the morning prayer and after the afternoon prayer, while he is within the time of the obligatory prayer: does he pray the rak'at of Tawaf as a supererogatory prayer, whether they were supererogatory or obligatory? He said, 'No.' And that which indicates that what the first report contained is specific to supererogatory prayers rather than obligatory ones is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: The afternoon (referring to Asr prayer time)
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: The morning (referring to Fajr prayer time)

ai.seo_question: Does one pray the two rak'at of Tawaf separately if done during the time of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Tawaf performed during the time of an obligatory prayer, ruling that the two rak'at of Tawaf are not offered as a separate supererogatory (nafl) prayer but are distinct from the wajib salat. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the ritual purity of Tawaf and the temporal obligations of daily prayers, ensuring that the performance of one does not inadvertently negate the specific legal status of the other. The text further reinforces that this specific prohibition applies to nafl acts, thereby preserving the integrity of fard (obligatory) prayers when combined with Tawaf.
